title: A Benchmark for Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination
hook: 13 LLMs try to explore, trade, craft, and build together in an open world — and most manage only ~6% of normalized return. Communication, not raw capability, turns out to be the biggest lever.
key_points: Tests LLM agents on open-ended multi-agent coordination: exploring, communicating, trading, crafting, building, fighting mobs together.
Across 13 modern LLMs, most agents average only around 6% normalized return.
On the hardest setting, zero-shot Gemini 3.1 Pro performs comparably to the best MARL agent trained for 1 billion environment steps.
Coordination emerges as a distinct bottleneck separate from long-horizon task competence.
Communication has the largest measured effect on performance in this harness.
content_html: Can LLM agents actually coordinate with each other in an open-ended world, not just follow a script? A new benchmark drops 13 modern LLMs into a shared environment where they must explore, communicate, trade resources, craft tools, build structures, and fight mobs together — and finds most of them still struggle badly.
extra_html: Per the author's summary on r/MachineLearning, agents average only around 6% normalized return across the benchmark, but the results aren't uniformly bleak: on the hardest setting, zero-shot Gemini 3.1 Pro performs comparably to the best multi-agent RL policy trained for a full billion environment steps — no task-specific training needed. The authors argue this shows coordination is a bottleneck distinct from an agent's raw long-horizon competence, and that communication between agents has the single largest effect on performance in their harness. Full details via the source link.

related.title: Multi-Agent LLMs Fail to Explore Each Other
related.hook: Drop LLM agents into a room together and they don't probe each other's abilities — they lock into narrow, polarized patterns that tank coordination and inflate regret.
